questions.question: TECH-SPEC.md:437 (Q8) says ctx_execute gets 'one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement (not 120s)'. I can't find the spike or number anywhere. Git archaeology: commit eea5877b (v1, Issue #406) REMOVED the fixed default entirely because it killed long Gradle/Maven/SBT builds, and made timeout optional with no server-side timer when the caller omits it. What exact millisecond value, and where is the measurement spike? If the value is too low, v2 re-breaks #406.
questions.why: ARCHAEOLOGY: INTRODUCED_BY eea5877b (2026-05-03, 'fix(opencode-plugin+executor+routing): Mickey 3-issue + Issue #406 timeout policy'). ORIGINAL_INTENT (commit msg): 'Server-side timeout policy is the wrong layer... Fix: Drop the Zod .default(...) from all three tools' timeout schemas... When the caller omits timeout, no server-side timer fires.' REGRESSION_RISK: v2's 'fixed default' directly contradicts the fix's own reasoning unless the new value is proven safe for long builds. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: need the measured value + spike file name before coding Q8.

questions.question: ADR-0002.md:47 (Q7) cites '#962' as the source for the retention size cap. I checked cm-main: commit 962d0cce is 'feat(stats): forward bytes_retrieved' — unrelated to retention/size caps. Is #962 an issue number (GitHub) or was this a sha typo? What is the actual size cap number (MB) and its source?
questions.why: Evidence check: `git log --all --oneline | grep 962` → only stats-related commits, none about retention. Citation looks wrong; without the real number I cannot implement the retention policy for M0.

questions.question: ADR-0002.md:46 (Q6) says 'the last server to close runs the WAL checkpoint, plus a checkpoint on close (v1 939c5ca8)'. Please confirm 939c5ca8 is the right sha (I have not yet located it in cm-main's visible history) and give the exact PRAGMA/checkpoint call plus how 'last server' is detected for the GP8 4-writer case (reference count? file lock? live PID list from Q7?).
questions.why: GP8 (TECH-SPEC:296) requires '4 servers + hooks writing one context.db, 0 busy errors, no retry loop'. Without the exact last-writer detection algorithm I can't implement the WAL checkpoint safely for M0 — a race here reproduces #985/#1213/#1248.

questions.question: ADR-0007 Q11 says 'no fallback chain' for project source per host and 'doctor reports a missing source'. What is the exact doctor output string/format when the source is missing, for each of Codex, Copilot CLI, and Remote-WSL specifically?
questions.why: Owner decision forbids fallback chains (hard rule), so the only user-facing behavior on a missing source is this doctor message. Without exact copy I'd have to invent wording, which risks violating the agent-issue-intake rule that AI agents must get maximum, precise debug data.

questions.question: ADR-0011/0013 (Q14) say main is protected 'by GitHub branch protection (pushes blocked), not by convention.' What are the exact branch protection settings to configure (required status checks list, required reviewers count, allow force-push=false, etc.) and is this applied via repo settings UI/API or as Terraform/script in the release skill?
questions.why: SKILL.md for /release needs this as a concrete M0 setup step; 'branch protection' alone isn't actionable without the rule set.

questions.question: Q18 says issue debug data strips only secrets ('tokens, .env values') and requires paths/logs/versions/transcript excerpts/doctor report. What is the exact secret-detection method (fixed regex list? entropy check? named env var allowlist?) and which transcript fields are mandatory in the issue form?
questions.why: This replaces ADR-0014's 'no path text' rule per the owner's own stated rule ('maksimum debug verisini gondermeli bize'). The issue template is AI-agent-facing (owner requirement) so the form schema needs the exact field list and the exact strip logic before I can draft it for M0.

questions.question: ADR-0010 Q16: ctx_upgrade mode:uninstall 'removes the cache... user data is kept unless the user confirms.' Since there is no separate CLI and this runs as an MCP tool call from inside a headless agent, how does the confirmation happen — a required tool argument (e.g. confirmDataRemoval:true), or an interactive host prompt? Which agents can even surface that prompt?
questions.why: Several v2 agents (Kiro, ZCode, Pi) only get tool descriptions, no interactive UI per TECH-SPEC. A confirm step that depends on host UI may silently fail on those agents.

questions.question: Q19: proxy env support (HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY) 'with an SSRF check on the target host.' What is the exact blocklist (RFC1918 ranges, 169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint, ::1/loopback, link-local IPv6) and does the check cover DNS rebinding (re-resolve after redirect) or only the first-hop hostname?
questions.why: TECH-SPEC:439 states the feature but not the check's scope. A metadata-endpoint or DNS-rebinding gap here is a real SSRF hole, and I need the exact rule set before writing the fetch wrapper for M0.
